title.narrative: Ensure the right to education for both boys and girls is protected, particularly those affected by drop-outs and who risk getting involved in violence either in or outside school

description.narrative: Education is not only an inalienable human right but also a pivotal component of Agenda 2030 for Sustainable Development, playing a vital role in fostering social inclusion and labour market participation. Furthermore, it serves as a linchpin in reconciling economic growth with equity, equality, justice and promoting active societal engagement. Latin America and the Caribbean stand out as the most unequal region globally, where stark inequalities in wealth distribution paint a sobering picture of societal inequity. At the apex of this inequality pyramid, the wealthiest 10% lay claim to a staggering 30% of the total income, while at the opposite end, the poorest 20% are left to contend with a mere 6% (GEM Report 2020). Despite a steady increase in school attendance and completion rates over the past two decades, particularly at the primary education level, there persists a troubling reality of exclusion for disadvantaged social groups. In this context, education is an empowering right in itself and one of the most powerful tools by which economically and socially marginalized children and adults can lift themselves out of poverty and participate fully in society. In light of these principles, this workplan is dedicated to equipping education systems with the tools and strategies necessary to safeguard the right to education for all children, irrespective of gender, with particular attention to dropped out and disengaged boys from education. By ensuring equitable participation in education, including of boys, governments in the region not only protect fundamental human rights but also promote social inclusion and empowerment, and then prevent those at risk of dropping out school and disengaging to get involved in violence in or outside school. Through comprehensive policies and programs, they should create inclusive learning environments that nurture the academic, social, and emotional development of every child, fostering a more equitable and prosperous society for generations to come.
